nodes.name: __main__.py
nodes.summary: CLI entry point for the DAG scheduler, invoked as `python -m runner`. Parses run scoping flags (--run-id, --phase, --node, --dry-run), loads the manifest graph and run context, optionally bootstraps phase prerequisites, dispatches the scheduler, and maps the run outcome onto four distinct process exit codes.
nodes.languageNotes: Python `__main__.py` package-executable convention; `load_dotenv()` is called at import time before any other runner import so transport configuration is present.

nodes.name: _parse_phase
nodes.summary: Normalizes the several accepted spellings of a --phase argument (`1`, `phase1`, `phase_01`) into a single integer phase number.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: The CLI driver: builds the argument parser, resolves repo root and manifest/library paths, enforces the mutual exclusion of --phase and --node, loads or initializes the RunContext, seeds phase prerequisites from durable Tier 4 gate evidence, runs the DAGScheduler, and translates RunSummary / RunAbortedError / DAGSchedulerError outcomes into exit codes 0-3.

nodes.name: agent_runtime.py
nodes.summary: The middle layer of the three-tier runtime stack: an orchestration adapter that loads agent and prompt specifications, resolves canonical tier inputs, sequences skill invocations through `run_skill()`, invokes Claude-free deterministic components, propagates failures, and determines `can_evaluate_exit_gate` by inspecting artifacts on disk. It never evaluates gates and never calls the scheduler.
nodes.languageNotes: The agent/prompt `.md` files it loads are specifications, not executable code — all domain reasoning happens inside the Claude invocations made by `run_skill()`.

nodes.name: AgentRuntimeError
nodes.summary: Exception raised for agent-runtime-layer faults such as a missing agent catalog entry or an unloadable prompt specification.

nodes.name: drafting_skills_superseded_by
nodes.summary: Returns the Phase-8 drafting skills that a given deterministic section assembler supersedes, so the monolithic drafter is not run when the assembler already composes the section from bounded sub-section drafts.

nodes.name: _load_agent_catalog
nodes.summary: Loads and caches `agent_catalog.yaml`, the authoritative registry of agent declarations (reads_from, writes_to, must_not) used to resolve inputs and constrain agent behavior.

nodes.name: _load_artifact_registry
nodes.summary: Loads the artifact schema specification so the runtime can map node IDs to the canonical artifact paths they produce and consume.

nodes.name: _load_prompt_spec
nodes.summary: Reads an agent's prompt specification Markdown file from disk, raising when the spec is absent.

nodes.name: _resolve_agent_inputs
nodes.summary: Resolves an agent's declared `reads_from` tier paths into concrete existing files on disk, expanding directory declarations and reporting which declared inputs are missing.

nodes.name: _resolve_skill_sequence
nodes.summary: Determines the ordered skill sequence for a node body from the manifest-resolved skill IDs, honoring suppression of drafting skills under reuse, preseed, or assembler supersession.

nodes.name: _resolve_budget_regime_safe
nodes.summary: Resolves the instrument's budget regime (lump-sum versus unit-cost) without raising, so skill applicability checks can degrade gracefully when the regime cannot be determined.
nodes.languageNotes: Reflects the instrument-conditional budget gate: lump-sum budgets come from the external planner, unit-cost budgets from a deterministic internal derivation.

nodes.name: _get_artifacts_produced_by_node
nodes.summary: Looks up every canonical artifact path a node is contractually expected to write, which is the basis for the on-disk gate-readiness check.

nodes.name: _determine_can_evaluate_exit_gate
nodes.summary: Decides whether the scheduler may evaluate the node's exit gate by inspecting actual file-system state for the gate-relevant artifacts, never by assuming that successful skill invocations imply artifact presence.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the constitutional rule that `can_evaluate_exit_gate` is derived from disk, not from optimistic assumption.

nodes.name: _get_exit_gate_for_node
nodes.summary: Reads the manifest to find which gate is bound as the given node's exit gate, so the runtime knows which artifacts are gate-relevant.

nodes.name: _resolve_instrument_type
nodes.summary: Resolves the active Horizon Europe instrument type (RIA/IA, CSA, MSCA, ERC and so on) from the Tier 3 call binding, which drives instrument-conditional skill applicability.

nodes.name: _context_sources_for
nodes.summary: Lists the upstream artifacts that must be passed as caller context into a given skill invocation.

nodes.name: _build_caller_context
nodes.summary: Assembles the caller-context payload handed to a skill invocation, reading the declared upstream artifacts from disk and threading prior-skill outputs through the sequence.

nodes.name: _missing_context_sources
nodes.summary: Returns the declared context sources that are absent from disk, so a skill is failed closed rather than invoked with incomplete context.

nodes.name: _resolve_auditable_artifact
nodes.summary: Identifies the artifact that an audit skill (traceability-check, compliance-check) should examine, so audit passes always target the authoritative section on disk even when drafting was skipped.

nodes.name: _check_skill_applicability
nodes.summary: Evaluates a skill's `applies_when` condition against the resolved instrument type and budget regime, so instrument-inapplicable skills are skipped rather than run against absent inputs.

nodes.name: run_agent
nodes.summary: The single public entry point of the agent runtime and the node body of every scheduler dispatch: it resolves the node's agent, inputs and skill sequence, runs decomposed drafting and deterministic components where bound, invokes each applicable skill through `run_skill()`, coordinates sub-agents and pre-gate agents, halts immediately on CONSTITUTIONAL_HALT, and returns an AgentResult carrying the invocation records and the disk-derived `can_evaluate_exit_gate` flag.
nodes.languageNotes: The only caller is the scheduler's `_dispatch_node()`; the function itself never evaluates a gate nor calls back into the scheduler.

nodes.name: _identify_agent_skills
nodes.summary: Resolves the skill IDs declared for an agent, used when the manifest node binding must be cross-checked against the agent catalog.

nodes.name: _refresh_inputs_from_outputs
nodes.summary: Folds the artifacts a skill just wrote back into the resolved input set, so later skills in the same node body see the freshly produced files.

nodes.name: _sub_agent_inputs_ready
nodes.summary: Checks on disk whether a sub-agent's or pre-gate agent's declared inputs are all present before that nested agent is coordinated within the same node body.

nodes.name: call_slicer.py
nodes.summary: The deterministic Step-0 input bounding pass: before any Claude invocation, it extracts the single target call entry from a large grouped work-programme JSON (338-794 KB) into a bounded ~5-10 KB call slice so downstream skills read only call-specific data. Pure Python with no Claude dependency and no domain reasoning.
nodes.languageNotes: Called once by `DAGScheduler.run()` before the dispatch loop; failure is non-blocking because skills fall back to reading the full grouped JSON.

nodes.name: CallSlicerError
nodes.summary: Exception raised when the call slice cannot be produced — missing selected-call binding, unknown work programme, no topic match, or a slice exceeding the 20 KB hard limit.

nodes.name: generate_call_slice
nodes.summary: Reads the Tier 3 selected call, locates its work programme in the grouped-JSON map, scans the destinations/calls structure for the matching topic code, and writes the bounded slice to `call_extracts/<topic_code>.slice.json`, failing closed when the result exceeds MAX_SLICE_BYTES.

nodes.name: checkpoint_publisher.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic node-body component that publishes the immutable Phase-8 `phase8_checkpoint.json` to Tier 4 after confirming the six Phase-8 gate results. Cross-run gate results are authorized by deterministic set membership against `accepted_upstream_gates` and recorded verbatim as a provenance quad, so the checkpoint stays auditable against durable evidence without re-stamping.
nodes.languageNotes: Replaces the retired `checkpoint-publish` skill once it was found to be entirely mechanical; the only non-deterministic field, `published_at`, is excluded from the byte-equal replay invariant.

nodes.name: CheckpointPublishError
nodes.summary: Exception raised on any structural fault — missing, malformed, non-pass or wrong-schema gate result, an unauthorized cross-run gate, or an attempt to overwrite an already-published checkpoint.

nodes.name: _read_json_dict
nodes.summary: Reads a required JSON object from disk, raising CheckpointPublishError when the file is missing, unreadable, or not a JSON object.

nodes.name: _validate_gate_result
nodes.summary: Confirms that a durable gate result artifact carries the expected schema ID and a `status: pass` verdict before the checkpoint may assert the gate passed.

nodes.name: _authorize_and_build_quad
nodes.summary: Authorizes a gate result whose durable run_id differs from the current run by deterministic set membership against `accepted_upstream_gates`, then copies the provenance quad (gate_id, original_run_id, evidence_path, input_fingerprint, versions) verbatim from the durable result.

nodes.name: _build_tier3_snapshot
nodes.summary: Captures the Tier 3 project-instantiation state referenced by the checkpoint so the published record identifies exactly which project data the Phase-8 outcome was built on.

nodes.name: publish_checkpoint
nodes.summary: The component entry point for node n08f: validates all six Phase-8 gate results, authorizes any cross-run evidence, assembles the checkpoint document with its optional `inherited_gate_provenance` array, and atomically writes the immutable artifact — refusing to overwrite a checkpoint already marked published.

nodes.name: dag_scheduler.py
nodes.summary: The top layer of the runtime stack and the largest module in the repository: it builds a read-only ManifestGraph from the compiled manifest, runs a synchronous dispatch loop over the DAG, and owns gate evaluation exclusively. Each dispatch follows the five-step contract (set running, entry gate, node body via run_agent, exit gate, NodeExecutionResult), propagates HARD_BLOCK to Phase 8 on budget-gate failure, and writes a durable RunSummary on every exit path.
nodes.languageNotes: Explicitly forbidden from calling `run_skill()` directly; all skill execution flows through the agent runtime, and the exit gate is skipped if and only if the entry gate failed, the agent body failed, or `can_evaluate_exit_gate` is False.

nodes.name: _gate_result_repo_path
nodes.summary: Resolves a gate ID to its canonical repo-relative Tier 4 gate result path via the gate result registry.

nodes.name: format_unsatisfied_condition
nodes.summary: Renders an unsatisfied DAG incoming condition as a human-readable line for CLI and summary output.

nodes.name: format_evidence_violation
nodes.summary: Renders a predecessor-evidence violation dict (node, gate, evidence path, reason code) as a readable diagnostic line.

nodes.name: verify_released_predecessors
nodes.summary: Re-verifies every transitively upstream `released` predecessor against its durable Tier 4 exit-gate result — present, schema-valid, status pass, and content-fresh — because a persisted state string in `.claude/runs/` is runtime memory rather than source truth. Read-only and scheduler-side: it writes nothing and returns one violation dict per unproven claim so a scoped step fails closed.

nodes.name: _collect_upstream_nodes
nodes.summary: Recursively accumulates all transitive upstream node IDs for a target set by tracing incoming conditions, terminating on acyclic graphs via a visited set.

nodes.name: bootstrap_phase_prerequisites
nodes.summary: Seeds upstream prerequisite nodes as `released` in a fresh RunContext from durable Tier 4 gate evidence, so `--phase N` execution can proceed with a new run-id per invocation. This is a bootstrap step run before dispatch, not resume logic — readiness still derives from current RunContext state.

nodes.name: DAGSchedulerError
nodes.summary: Base exception for scheduler configuration faults such as an empty phase scope, an unmatched node scope, or a dispatched node with no exit gate defined.

nodes.name: RunSummary
nodes.summary: Typed dataclass capturing the full outcome of a run — overall status, node states in manifest order, terminal nodes reached, stalled and hard-blocked nodes, the gate results index, and per-node failure details. It computes scope-aware status for `--phase` and `--node` runs and writes `run_summary.json` before `run()` returns or raises.

nodes.name: RunAbortedError
nodes.summary: Raised when in-scope nodes remain pending after the dispatch loop exits; carries the already-built RunSummary on `.summary` so the CLI can still report the run.

nodes.name: IncomingCondition
nodes.summary: Immutable record of one DAG edge condition: the source node whose release unblocks the target, as declared in the manifest.

nodes.name: ManifestGraph
nodes.summary: Read-only in-memory graph built from `manifest.compile.yaml`: exposes canonical node IDs, entry and exit gate bindings, terminal flags, incoming conditions, readiness checks against current RunContext state, phase membership, and resolution of `--node` scope from canonical IDs or phase+substep shorthand.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler
nodes.summary: The synchronous dispatch loop and sole owner of gate evaluation. `run()` generates the Step-0 call slice, iterates ready nodes, and settles stalled ones; `_dispatch_node()` implements the five-step contract — set running, evaluate entry gate, execute the node body via `run_agent()`, evaluate the exit gate, return a NodeExecutionResult — applying Phase-8 preseed and reuse decisions, suppressing draft-consuming components, propagating HARD_BLOCK from the budget gate, and reloading RunContext after every gate evaluation.
nodes.languageNotes: Failure origins form a closed set of three (`entry_gate`, `agent_body`, `exit_gate`) and are persisted alongside node state; node states are `pending`, `running`, `released`, `blocked_at_entry`, `blocked_at_exit`, `deterministic_pass_semantic_pending`, `hard_block_upstream`.
